chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh said: Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Sahil narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Fazari who said: Muhammad ibn Humran al-Mad'ini narrated to us from Ziyad al-Qandi who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: O Ziyad, I love for you what I love for my self and I dislike for you what I dislike for my self. Complete the prayer in the two sanctuaries, in Kufa, and near the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَتِمَّ الصَّلَاةَ: Complete the prayer (performing four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa (a major city in Iraq with significant Shia shrines)
key_terms.قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Where should Muslims complete their four-rak'ah prayer instead of shortening it?
ai.summary: Although the provided chain of narration (isnad) in *Al-Istibsar* traces back through Muhammad ibn Humran to Ziyad al-Qandi, the text is traditionally cited as a hadith of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who addresses Ziyad with the famous maxim 'I love for you what I love for myself.' This narration establishes the jurisprudential ruling of 'itmam' (praying four rak'ahs instead of two) in the specific sanctuaries of Mecca, Medina, Kufa, and the shrine of Imam al-Husayn, distinguishing these locations from general travel contexts. The inclusion of Kufa and Karbala highlights the unique spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrines in Shia jurisprudence, where the prayer is completed regardless of the traveler's distance or intent.
